pr_title: Add more weapon burst controls and simplify RA Vulcan setup
pr_body:
Added more configurability for burst behavior to `WeaponInfo`.

Closes #13220.
Fixes #18312.
pr_comments:
> Added a `BurstMode` enum to `WeaponInfo`, with the `AllOnInitialTargetPosition` option allowing to replicate RA's `Vulcan` behavior without the yaml-heavy work-around of using tons of delayed warheads.

Nuke weapons also have a ton of delayed warheads

> Nuke weapons also have a ton of delayed warheads

This cannot be applied to nukes, they're a different beast.
Each burst would trigger all warheads, including the explosion effect.

It only works for the Vulcan because the warheads at each delay were otherwise 100% identical, and triggering the piffpiff effect each time is fine and actually intended.

> I've put less thought into this than you have, but given those use cases my first thought would to be use separate flags:

Done, although I left out `BurstResetOnTargetChange` for now since that would complicate things further and isn't needed for the Vulcan refactor. I'll probably file a follow-up once this is merged.

> It would be ideal if we could also fix `FireDelay` to update the target position if `BurstTracking = true`

Done.
Do we understand what broke #18312 and how this fixes it? My main worry is if we don't then there may be other weapons that we haven't yet realized are broken.

> Do we understand what broke #18312 and how this fixes it? My main worry is if we don't then there may be other weapons that we haven't yet realized are broken.

Looks to me like #18068. If you test with combat geometry only the first of six shots hits. By merging the rules for the other shots into the first one this PR fixes the problem.

> Do we understand what broke #18312 and how this fixes it? My main worry is if we don't then there may be other weapons that we haven't yet realized are broken.

Yes, I forgot to properly update the ValidTargets on the delayed duplicate warheads. With the new setup there's only the original damage warhead, which doesn't have that issue.

> Can we please change this so that all of the cases use the !bulkScheduleBarrels logic?

The reason I haven't responded so far is that unless I'm missing something, this would pretty much mean throwing out the core part of this PR altogether, trying to find a completely different approach and (if I even succeed with the latter) rewriting the bulk behavior from scratch.
What I have here is the only working approach I was able to come up with though, so that would essentially boil down to giving up for now and deferring this to the undefined 'Future' again.

I currently have no time/motivation for this (especially if the current approach isn't good enough and everything needs to be redone from scratch with a new conceptual approach), so to clean up the PR queue and Next milestone a bit I'm moving this to Future for now.

issue_context.title: Pillbox damage has regressed (bleed)
issue_context.body: Pillboxes now take 4-5 bursts to kill riflemen instead of 1-2. This is likely a TargetTypes regression. Although that should be an easy fix, we might want to wait on #18170 instead.
comments:
The problem is that weapons rely on inheriting `ValidTargets: GroundActor, WaterActor` definitions from their default (e.g. `^HeavyMG`) template. This works for `Warhead@1Dam`, but not any others. `Vulcan` defines 5 additional warheads that are now missing `ValidTargets` definitions and therefore don't work.

#18170 covers the pillboxes, but we should check that no other weapons have the same problem before we allow that to close this issue.
I played around a bit with every combat unit, defense structure,  and superweapon; comparing bleed and release side to side. I did not see any more damage disparities.

review_comments: Camo pillboxes no longer uncloak while attacking, so the implementation in `Armament` is somehow not covering this case!
I guess that `Armament` will be notifying the passenger, while this is needed to notify the pillbox. Adding this back to just `AttackGarrisoned` should hopefully be sufficient.
Style nit: Never use `else if` after a return - `if` is sufficient because we have already returned if the earlier branch was taken.
Why don't we need to update `currentBarrel` here?

`currentBarrel` is only used for weapons with Burst == 1 to toggle the LocalOffsets.

Bulk scheduling only makes sense and therefore is only enabled/supported for Burst > 1, so there's no reason to update it.

`i` is never equal to 0, so pillboxes (and other actors with weapons that rely on `StartBurstReport`) never play their firing audio. `i == Weapon.Burst` will do what you want, but see my overall comment above.
